title: Model Comparison & Decision Workshop - Axiom Labs
summary: Redwood ran through the model catalog UI and API workflow for selecting open models, interpreting benchmark outputs, and using the compatibility matrix to pick runtime variants. Customer cares about inference cost, latency SLOs for sub-200ms 1k token prompt, private data controls (VPC + KMS), and a short pilot to evaluate quality vs quantized 8-bit variants.
topics: Benchmarks: latency vs throughput vs quality
next_steps: Redwood to share tailored pilot proposal and pricing by 2026-11-06
SE to run a 3-model benchmark with Axiom sample prompts and share results (week of 11/9)
Send security pack + SOC2 docs and network diagram link
action_items: Maya Patel - send pilot pricing + SOW draft - 2026-11-06
Jonas Reed - run latency/throughput bench with Axiom prompts and share CSV - 2026-11-12
Marcus Lee - provide sample prompt set and traffic pattern spreadsheet - 2026-11-05
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 PST | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Sara (Axiom CTO), Marcus (ML Platform), Diego (Infra), Lina (NLP)

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to make today pretty hands-on — walk through the model catalog UI, show how benchmarks land on the compatibility matrix, and talk about a small pilot. Quick intros?

[00:12] Sara (Axiom): Hi, Sara here. CTO at Axiom Labs. We're evaluating options to replace our current in-house endpoint stack — mostly wanting lower TCO and predictable SLA for chat assistants.

[00:20] Marcus: Marcus here, I run ML infra. We care about autoscaling behavior and how Redwood handles KV cache for stateful chat.

[00:28] Jonas (SE): Awesome. I'll jump into the demo — I'll share my screen. We're on the Redwood Console, model catalog tab.

[00:40] [screen share sound] Jonas: First thing you'll see is the main filter bar. Customers like you will use tags — "latency-sensitive", "quant-8", "cpu-friendly". I can toggle quality bands, and it will re-rank models based on your selected metric.

[01:05] Lina (Axiom): Quick question — when you say re-rank, is that live for the tenant, or just a UI sort?

[01:11] Jonas: Good call. It's a view-level re-rank by default. If you pin a profile or create a deployment policy, that config becomes enforceable at routing time. So you can say route 80% to high-quality variant and 20% to quantized cheaper variant.

[01:30] Diego (Infra): How do kernel mappings show up? We run on mixed GPU types and want to know which models fall back to TF32 vs INT8 optimized kernels.

[01:42] Jonas: On the compatibility matrix we annotate each model X hardware cell with the preferred kernel family and the expected memory footprint. There's also a note if we recommend a different checkpoint for improved INT8 behavior. Example: a7-large has a different kernel on A100 vs H100.

[02:05] Marcus: And for latency SLOs — can we set per-route SLOs and get automatic fallback if the model breaches 95th percentile?

[02:15] Priya (Product): Yes, you can define route-level SLOs. We support automatic fallback policies: cross-model fallback, or region fallback, or capacity-tier fallback. You can attach a quality threshold so fallback only happens if output QA passes a prompt-set test.

[02:45] Sara: That sounds powerful. We're also concerned about total token cost — we often hit long context windows. How do we estimate cost with prefix/KV caching in place?

[02:56] Jonas: The Optimize tab provides a token-level cost breakdown. For cached prefixes we show effective tokens served vs billed tokens and estimated savings. There's also a simulated run — you can upload sample sessions and get projected monthly bills.

[03:18] Lina: Can we run a bench with our 1k token average convo and get 95p latency numbers for a few model variants?

[03:25] Jonas: Absolutely. That's one of the next steps we suggested. We'll run three variants: a higher-quality fp16 baseline, an 8-bit quant variant, and a compressed L2 variant. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and throughput.

[03:40] [10-second pause; typing noise]

[03:51] Jonas: Jumping back to the compatibility matrix — see these colored cells: green means full runtime match; amber indicates we can serve but with performance caveats; red means unsupported kernels. Hover reveals notes and a link to the bench.

[04:10] Marcus: How deterministic are those bench numbers? We need to include them in a procurement RFP.

[04:18] Maya (AE): Good point. We attach bench metadata — hardware type, model checksum, sequence length distribution, and batching policy used. We also include a CSV export you can drop into your RFP appendix.

[04:35] Sara: About security - we operate in regulated workflows. We need VPC private deployment and keys in our KMS. How does Redwood Private look?

[04:45] Priya: Redwood Private runs the control plane with connectors to your VPC; data plane can be customer-managed. We integrate with most KMSes and HSMs, and provide audit logs per token. SOC2 report is available, and we can produce network diagrams.

[05:10] Diego: For audit logs, is token-level content logged or just metadata? We cannot persist PII content.

[05:18] Priya: By default, we log metadata and hashes; content can be redacted or disabled. Private deployments allow you to keep logs on-prem. We'll include details in the security pack.

[05:35] Lina: Back to model quality — how do we compare against our eval sets? Can we attach custom evals?

[05:42] Jonas: Yes — Console supports custom eval sets tied to model versions. You can run batch evals, and we show failure modes and example outputs. We also support diff view between two checkpoints so you can see regression heatmaps.

[06:05] Sara: If we do a pilot, what's the minimum time window? We want to hit realistic traffic patterns.

[06:12] Maya: Typical pilots are 2-4 weeks. For latency-sensitive apps we prefer 3 weeks to capture variability and run the p95/p99 profile. The pilot can be on Dedicated reserved capacity or Private depending on your security needs.

[06:30] Marcus: Cost-wise, is there a trial credit? And for Dedicated, how does bursting work?

[06:38] Maya: We offer limited credits for pilots. Dedicated supports burst pools — you reserve baseline capacity and configure burst to grow up to a multiple for short periods. We can show cost modeling under Optimize.

[06:55] [screen scroll noise] Jonas: I'm going to open the Benchmarks tab — here's the bench for our recommended shortlist. Notice we show quality on the Y-axis and normalized cost on the X-axis. Each point links to a detailed run with hardware info.

[07:20] Lina: That scatter is helpful. Are the quality metrics single-number or composite?

[07:25] Jonas: You can view the composite or drill into sub-metrics — factuality, instruction-following, latency-sensitive score, hallucination rate. For your purposes we can create a custom composite that weights factuality and latency.

[07:48] Diego: On the engineering side, what's the integration path — do we call the Redwood API directly or use a sidecar? What's the SDK story?

[07:58] Jonas: Two main paths: host via Redwood API or Private deploy with our runtime endpoints inside your VPC. SDKs in Python/Node are thin wrappers. We also provide a gRPC path for lower overhead.

[08:15] Marcus: Is streaming supported end-to-end with private? We need real-time token streaming for our chat UI.

[08:22] Priya: Yes, streaming is supported for hosted and private runtimes. We maintain backpressure and support multipart SSE or gRPC streaming.

[08:40] Sara: Can we see a quick example of routing rules? We want to route based on user tier: free users go to cheaper quant models, premium users to high-quality variants, with auto-fallback if p95 > 350ms.

[08:52] Jonas: Sure — in the Routes tab we have policy builder. You add predicates (user.tier == premium), then actions (route to model X), and attach fallback policy: if p95 > 350ms then send to model Y. There's also a canary rollout slider.

[09:15] Lina: What about model pinning and rollbacks? We need fast rollback on regressions.

[09:21] Jonas: We support version pinning and instant rollback. When you detect regression, you can revert traffic with one click and run differential evals to diagnose.

[09:36] [slight audio overlap, someone coughs]

[09:45] Maya: Let's talk bench run specifics for the pilot. Jonas, can you outline what you'll run?

[09:51] Jonas: We'll run three models across two hardware points: H100 and A100. For each model we'll run 1k token sessions replicated to match your concurrency profile. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and GPU memory utilization. We'll also run the custom eval set Lina provides to score quality.

[10:15] Marcus: For concurrency, aim for our expected peak QPS ~ 80 concurrent sessions. We'll send the spreadsheet after the call.

[10:25] Jonas: Perfect. We'll also try batching policies — continuous batching vs fixed batches — to see cost/latency tradeoffs.

[10:38] Sara: One more on compliance: can you produce a signed DPA and meet our data residency needs in EU region?

[10:46] Priya: Yes, we have EU regions and can sign DPA with standard clauses. For Private deployments, the control plane runs in our managed zone while data plane stays in your region. We'll add the legal contact in the follow-up email.

[11:05] Lina: I noticed earlier the compatibility matrix flagged a model as amber due to tokenizer differences. How often are tokenizers reconciled?

[11:12] Jonas: Tokenizer mismatches are usually surfaced by our onboarding tests. For those we recommend either a tokenizer shim or a small finetune to ensure alignment. We document exact tokenizer versions in the model metadata.

[11:30] [typing] Jonas: I'm going to open an actual bench run — here's model "rwd-a7-large-fp16" on H100: p95 210ms for 1k tokens with our default batching. The quant-8 variant shows p95 145ms but quality delta of -3.2% on your custom eval.

[11:58] Sara: That tradeoff seems plausible. What's the billing difference roughly?

[12:04] Maya: In that example quant-8 reduces token cost by ~42% in our model loop due to lower compute and memory. Exact numbers in the bench CSV.

[12:18] Diego: For private deployment — who maintains the runtime updates and kernel upgrades?

[12:25] Priya: We offer two models: managed runtime (we push updates on a controlled cadence) or customer-managed runtime image where you control upgrades. For critical environments you can approve updates in a staging lane first.

[12:45] Marcus: Are you able to run a head-to-head with our current in-house endpoint to show delta on cost per 1k tokens?

[12:53] Jonas: Yes — we can ingest a short trace from your system and run a simulated billing comparison. That would be part of the bench deliverable.

[13:05] [screen pause]

[13:12] Sara: Ok, summary questions: 1) pilot timeline 2-3 weeks; 2) privacy - VPC/KMS supported; 3) we'll need SOC2 + DPA; 4) run three-model bench with our prompts and concurrency; 5) pricing and SOW. Anything missing?

[13:28] Maya: That matches. I'll send the SOW and pricing. Jonas will run the bench. Priya will attach security docs.

[13:36] Lina: On the quality delta - is there a tool to visualize token-level hallucinations?

[13:42] Jonas: We have an annotation tool that highlights hallucinated spans across prompts and aggregates by token position and intent class. We'll include a sample output in the bench.

[13:57] Marcus: A couple technical clarifications for the bench CSV: include GPU perf counters, batch size, and kernel flags used. We need to replicate results internally.

[14:10] Maya: Noted — Jonas will include those fields.

[14:18] [brief pause]

[14:20] Diego: Small ops question — what observability hooks exist for tracing across Redwood and our app?

[14:27] Priya: We support distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry and provide tracing headers. You can correlate request ids and token timing between services.

[14:40] Sara: Great. If we move forward, who will be our Redwood customer success contact?

[14:46] Maya: I'll be primary AE; once pilot starts you'll be handed to a CSM — typically named in the SOW.

[14:55] Lina: When can we expect the bench results?

[14:58] Jonas: If you share prompts and traffic by Thursday 11/5, we can run benches the week of 11/9 and deliver by 11/12.

[15:09] Sara: That works. Final quick thing — are there any gotchas for long context (>8k) use?

[15:14] Jonas: For long contexts, watch memory pressure and KV cache effectiveness. We recommend progressive summarization for older history and we can show cost projections in Optimize.

[15:27] Maya: Ok, let's recap and wrap. Next steps: pricing + SOW by 11/6, Axiom to send prompts + traffic by 11/5, SE bench deliverable by 11/12, security pack today/tomorrow.

[15:45] Sara: Thanks all. Appreciate the clarity.

[15:50] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links to the bench template and a calendar invite for the kick-off.

[15:58] [meeting ended]

Note: rough transcription, occasional audio overlap, speaker attributions approximate. Links mentioned: Security pack (link shared in chat: https://redwood.example.com/security/axiom-pack), bench CSV template (https://redwood.example.com/bench-template.csv), SOW draft placeholder (internal link).
